newsitem.title: USA: Justice Department sues University of Minnesota.
newsitem.headline: Justice Department sues University of Minnesota.

text.p: The United States has filed a suit alleging that the University of Minnesota falsely obtained and misused federal grants and received illegal Medicare payments, the Justice Department said on Friday.

The department filed a complaint seeking unspecified damages under seal in U.S. District Court in Minneapolis on Thursday, after failing to reach a settlement with the university during over a year of negotiations.
The court removed the seal on Friday.

The government's complaint contained a range of allegations, including that the university submitted false claims and false statements when seeking federal grant monies in connection with at least 30 federal grants.

"The University of Minnesota receives over $100 million a year from the National Institutes of Health alone and must use those funds subject to the requirement of the law," said Assistant Attorney General Frank Hunger.
The department is also asking the court to order the university to return what it says were millions of dollars in profits the university earned illegally by selling ALG, antilymphocyte globulin.

ALG is an immunosuppressive drug used after transplant surgery, especially kidney transplants, to prevent the patient's body from rejecting the new organ. The Justice Department said the drug was not licensed for commercial sale.
